draft.title: Tone
card: Tone is the writer's attitude to the subject, which comes through in the words. Playful, bitter, serious, gentle and admiring are all tones.
Word choice is the main clue. Compare "The old car coughed and died" with "The vehicle ceased to function". The first sounds warm and a little humorous. The second sounds cold and official.
To name a tone, ask how the writer seems to feel about the subject. Look at the words that carry feeling, such as sneered, adored or merely.
Tone affects how a reader responds. A mocking tone can make us laugh at a character, while a respectful tone can make us take the character seriously.
draft.remember: Tone is the writer's attitude, and the word choices are the clues to it.

a.q: Which of these best describes what tone is in a piece of writing?
opts: The writer's attitude to the subject, shown in the words
The place and time in which the story is set
The order in which the events of the story happen
The main message that the writer wants readers to learn
a.why: Tone is the attitude the writer shows towards the subject, and it comes through in word choice. Theme is the message a reader takes from a text, so it is a tempting mistake, but it is a different idea.
a.clue: Think about how the writer seems to feel.

b.q: Read this sentence: "Dad proudly unveiled his masterpiece, a crooked shed." The writer adds that it leaned like a tired giraffe. Which tone does the writing show?
b.why: The comparison to a tired giraffe and the word masterpiece for a crooked shed poke fun at Dad in a friendly way, so the tone is gently mocking. It is not bitter, because nothing in the words suggests anger or resentment.
b.clue: Look at how the shed is described, and ask whether the writer is angry or amused.

a.best: The writer's attitude to the subject, shown in the words
